findings.dimension_name: seedDefaults error masking potential diagnostic issues
findings.title: seedDefaults masks diagnostic information about system failures
findings.body: The seedDefaults fallback at lines 150-152 silently converts potential diagnostic information into a default-seeded value, hiding critical system issues. When result == nil (indicating a fundamental API/auth/provider failure) or result.Parsed == nil due to unexpected errors, the code returns a default value with nil error instead of propagating the diagnostic information. This violates the error handling principle that billing/auth/provider failures should not be hidden behind default values.
findings.evidence:
Step 1: app.Harness returns result, err where result could be nil due to API failures
Step 2: fatal.CheckFatalHarnessError already filters out some fatal errors at line 137
Step 3: But if result is nil due to non-fatal but diagnostic-worthy errors, line 150 triggers seedDefaults
Step 4: Line 151 returns &seeded, result, nil - masking the fact that result was nil and hiding potentially important diagnostic information
Step 5: Callers like Run cannot distinguish between successful execution and system failures that were masked by defaults
findings.suggestion: Add diagnostic information preservation before seedDefaults fallback. Either: 1) Keep the original result when result == nil to preserve diagnostic information, or 2) Add error context in the result.FailureType to distinguish actual failures from fallback scenarios, ensuring diagnostic errors are not masked as successful default-seeded responses.
